title: Database-enforced idempotency key
summary: Persist a stable business idempotency key and enforce uniqueness at the approval_outbox boundary.
mechanism: Derive or receive one stable approval-intent key, store it with the outbox row, and use a database unique constraint plus insert-or-read handling so concurrent equivalent requests converge on one committed durable effect.

data_changes: Add idempotency_key column and unique constraint

behavioral_effects.current_behavior: Equivalent requests can independently commit separate outbox rows.
behavioral_effects.target_behavior: Equivalent requests carrying the same business intent converge on one committed outbox row and one business result.
intentionally_changed_behavior: The second equivalent durable insert is rejected or resolved to the existing result.

transaction_semantics: The unique check and outbox write execute in the existing transaction; a uniqueness conflict is converted into a read of the already committed or concurrently committed business result.
concurrency_semantics: Database uniqueness is the final serialization point across processes and nodes.
failure_semantics: A conflicting equivalent request returns the same business outcome; a conflicting non-equivalent payload for the same key fails explicitly as an idempotency conflict.

compatibility.api: No required public shape change when the key is derived from an existing stable business identifier; an explicit header would require separate approval.
compatibility.event: One producer outbox event per key; event schema can remain unchanged if the key is producer metadata.
compatibility.data: Existing rows require a safe nullable-to-backfilled migration strategy.
compatibility.deployment: Mixed-version deployment must avoid old writers bypassing the final NOT NULL enforcement.
compatibility.operational: Uniqueness conflicts and idempotency conflict rates require metrics.

security.impact: The key must not expose sensitive business data and must be scoped to the correct tenant or authorization domain.
threats_considered: Replay with reused key and altered payload

migration.strategy: Add nullable key, deploy dual-compatible writers, backfill where derivable, create unique index after duplicate assessment, then enforce requiredness for new writes.
migration.backfill: Derive keys only where business identity is unambiguous; quarantine historical ambiguous duplicates.
migration.rollout: Expand-migrate-contract with observability before constraint enforcement.
migration.mixed_version_behavior: Old writers remain a temporary risk until all instances write the key; final constraint activation occurs only after fleet convergence.

rollback.strategy: Disable application conflict resolution and stop writing the key before dropping the constraint; preserve the column for forensic recovery.
rollback.data_recovery: No committed approval data must be deleted during rollback.
rollback.point_of_no_return: External consumers relying on strict single-event semantics may make semantic rollback unsafe.

success_indicators: No two committed rows for one key
failure_indicators: Constraint conflicts with different payload fingerprints
Rows written without keys after enforcement date

verification_strategy.method: Run concurrent equivalent requests against a real database and query committed outbox rows.
verification_strategy.expected_result: Exactly one row is committed and both callers observe the same business result.
verification_strategy.evidence_produced: Test command, database query output, transaction logs.

verification_strategy.method: Run API contract and compatibility tests with existing clients.
verification_strategy.expected_result: Request and response contracts remain compatible.
verification_strategy.evidence_produced: Contract-test report and serialized payload diff.

benefits: Guarantee resides at durable effect boundary

residual_risks.description: Historical rows may not have a uniquely derivable business key.
residual_risks.mitigation: Use nullable expansion and quarantine ambiguous historical records.

decision_requirements.question: Should the idempotency key be client supplied or derived from an existing business identifier?
decision_requirements.recommended_choice: Server derived when an approved stable business identifier exists.
decision_requirements.basis: Avoids public contract change while preserving stable retry identity.

falsification_conditions: No stable business intent identifier can be derived or accepted.
The deployed database cannot provide the required uniqueness guarantee.
